For candidate execution 087adee8e8a24fe88e5c85fe89e638c8 the selected plans view (updates 0,5,10,15,20,25,30,34) records per-update effective_horizon = 10 control intervals at sampled updates 5 (F651), 10 (F469) and 20 (F686), and reduced values only at the two latest sampled updates: 5 at update 30 (F658) and 1 at update 34 (F691). With a 0.01 s control period (F219) and 0.35 s simulated duration (F348) these reductions equal the remaining task time in control intervals (0.05 s -> 5; 0.01 s -> 1), i.e. a receding-horizon-to-terminal effect rather than persistent truncation.

In the same sampled plans view optimization_raw_status is a budget/iteration-limited stop at every sampled update and never a converged solve: update 5 (F673), update 15 (F710) and update 30 (F661) record User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible (F675, F713, F647, F659), and the candidate stopping counts User_Requested_Stop = 34 (F681) plus Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded = 1 (F697) sum to the 35 applied control updates (F426, F518).

Applied control updates are distinct from optimized selections in the sampled view: optimization_selected_iteration is 0 at update 0 (F655), the run records initialization_selected = 29 (F671, F680) with noninitialization_selected = 6 (F715), while the late sampled updates 30 and 34 record selected_iteration 39 (F648) and 68 (F704); most applied control updates therefore reused an initialization plan under a spent budget.

Computation wall time stays far above the simulated step: mean_update_s = 17.77877309145406 s (F703) against a 0.01 s control period (F219) with deadline_misses = 35 (F464, F511), consistent with a saturated solve budget; wall overruns do not imply skipped simulated steps or injected actuator delay.
